title: Intelligence community split on Havana syndrome
place_text: US intelligence community, State Department, CIA

tellings.quote:
But I think there was not unonymity
within the community, the intelligence
community on what was going on.

plain: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, says the US intelligence services were not of one mind about Havana syndrome. That is the name for unexplained illnesses reported by American diplomats and spies, first in Cuba. Haseltine tells Michels that there was no agreement across the State Department, the CIA and the wider intelligence world about what was causing it.
